requirements.evidence: Contract met: CallMode enum (app/Enums/CallMode.php:5-9), NoWaitingTicketsException extends RuntimeException (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7), invokable action with the right signature (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:17-21). Queue row locked and is_active read from the locked copy (25-32); ordering priority desc/issued_at/id (106-108); priority_only `priority > 0` (78-81), normal_only `priority = 0` oldest first (83-85); fairness over the last 3 by called_at desc, id desc with a normal-waiting check (117-133); candidate locked and re-checked with skip-and-retry (44-51); only status/called_at/called_by_user_id set, and the saved model is returned (53-58). Edge case: the fairness history filters `status = Called` (119), so tickets that later leave the `called` status would drop out of the history; `whereNotNull('called_at')` would be more robust.

conventions.evidence: Domain write lives in app/Actions as one invokable class, matching the convention. docs/business-rules.md and docs/architecture.md are updated as the task requires. CHANGELOG.md is not updated under [Unreleased], and there is no PHPDoc on the public __invoke; conventions.md asks for both.

security.evidence: The task says no authorization (trusted caller), and the docs state this (architecture.md:237-238). No user input is mass-assigned: fields are set explicitly (CallNextTicket.php:53-56). Transactional locking prevents double calls. No weakness found.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php covers ordering and the id tie-break (lines 52-78), each mode (80-106), fairness trigger, fewer than 3 calls, reset, priority_only history, and no normal waiting (108-181), other queues and called tickets (183-193), a stale inactive queue (195-207), the dataset of no-eligible cases (209-225), and write-once fields (227-243). The lost-race skip path (candidate already called after selection) has no test, and the docs link IssueTicketTest for the single-call invariant, which this diff doesn't show.

simplicity.evidence: Lean, with small private helpers. The selection query itself is `lockForUpdate()` (CallNextTicket.php:88), so the candidate row is already locked before the second explicit lock-and-recheck (44-47). The double locking is somewhat redundant, and on MySQL a locking read over the ordered scan can lock more rows than needed.

readability.evidence: Clear names (nextCandidateId, applyAnyOrdering, fairnessRequiresNormal), comments explain the locking rationale (23-24, 41-43, 66-67), and there is no dead code or debug output. The test helpers have descriptive names.

scope.evidence: The diff has only the action, enum, exception, tests and the two docs files the task requires. There is no HTTP, Livewire or authorization code.

issues.explanation: The fairness history only counts tickets still in status `called`. Once tickets move to a later status (served, done), they drop out of the last-3-calls history; filtering on `called_at IS NOT NULL` would match the rule's intent.
No test covers the lock-and-recheck skip path, where the candidate was called concurrently and the next ticket must be chosen.
CHANGELOG.md has no [Unreleased] entry for the new action, which the docs-sync convention requires.
The selection query is already a locking read, so the separate candidate lock is redundant, and on MySQL the ordered locking scan may lock more rows than needed.
The public __invoke has no PHPDoc describing its exceptions (InactiveQueueException, NoWaitingTicketsException).

review.summary: The change adds CallNextTicket, the CallMode enum and NoWaitingTicketsException, with correct queue locking, deterministic ordering, per-mode filtering, the fairness rule and a candidate re-check, plus thorough Pest tests and updated docs. Remaining gaps are small: the fairness history depends on status staying `called`, the concurrent-skip path has no test, and CHANGELOG/PHPDoc are missing. Approve with nits.
